chapter: Long Island years and Battle's estate
title: Edgar Battle's handling of his money
summary: Battle, raised partly in Durham's family, treated Durham's money as his own and gave no statements after 1959.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: : Well, I mean, I think Battle was a guy with good intentions, don't you?

I found out what he (inaudible) say, "He don't know what to do with no money. I'm going to use his money. When I get rich, I'll give him a lot of it, but give it to me." But he never get to that point. That was in his mind. I found that out later when he died. See, 50 percent and everything (inaudible), told his daughter, "You go to him and do what he say." (Inaudible) will to estate to my kids, you know, for music stuff. So I didn't say nothing (Inaudible) she wanted to do because he told her then. So the acknowledgement or the (inaudible) since 1959, he just (inaudible) ain't got time to get a statement. Say, "What do you want?" "Well, what do you want?" I say, "Well, I need a couple of -- (inaudible) $100? Two or three of what? So now I'd say, "Well, I'll take two or 300, let me have it."

He'd write a check, plus the check (inaudible) and give it to me. But he would never back up statement, so now I'm looking for a statement from 1959. It's the only way we can arrive, because his daughter, the lawyers are pushing her around and she's pushing me to start a lawsuit to try to get -- see what's happening on her end because she can't get the stuff in her hands right. (Inaudible) she ain't got but $7,000 showing.
Well, I don't know. So that's where -- when did you really sort of get closely associated with Edgar Battle?

He was raised up partly in my family, too, at the time when he got (inaudible). That's how he got in there. My mother raised him (inaudible). So, he feel like I'm a brother and he feel like he ought to take my money and do what he want to do with it.
